task_5.title: Fix stepwise plugin cache race condition with xdist workers
task_5.description: When pytest is run with the stepwise plugin and pytest-xdist, multiple worker nodes could simultaneously attempt to update the stepwise cache during session finalization. This race condition could corrupt the cache and cause performance degradation, particularly on network file systems like NFS with many worker nodes. The fix ensures that only the xdist controller process updates the stepwise cache, while worker processes skip cache writes entirely.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that the stepwise plugin's cache is not concurrently written to by multiple xdist worker processes during session teardown. Previously, when pytest was invoked with both --stepwise and xdist parallelization, every worker node attempted to write to the shared stepwise cache at session end, creating a race condition that could corrupt cached state and degrade performance on shared/network file systems.

expectation.grounded: When pytest runs with xdist, the pytest_sessionfinish hook at the module level and the StepwisePlugin.pytest_sessionfinish method must detect xdist worker processes by checking for the 'workerinput' attribute on the Config object. If the process is a worker, both functions must return early without calling Cache.set on the STEPWISE_CACHE_DIR key. Only the controller process should clear the stepwise cache (when stepwise is inactive) or persist the lastfailed list (when stepwise is active).
expectation.conceptual: When pytest runs in parallel via xdist, only the controller process should be responsible for updating the stepwise plugin's persistent cache. Worker processes must not write to the stepwise cache, ensuring that concurrent writes cannot corrupt the cache or cause file-system contention.

constraints.grounded: The stepwise cache must still be cleared by the controller process when the stepwise plugin is not active, and the lastfailed list must still be persisted by the controller when stepwise is active. The detection of xdist workers must rely on the presence of the 'workerinput' attribute on the Config object, which is the standard xdist mechanism for distinguishing workers from the controller. No other stepwise plugin behavior should be altered.
constraints.conceptual: Normal stepwise behavior in non-xdist runs must remain completely unchanged. The fix must only suppress cache writes from worker processes without affecting the controller's responsibility to maintain accurate stepwise state. The worker-detection mechanism must be compatible with the standard xdist worker identification convention.

behavior: In xdist worker processes, pytest_sessionfinish (module-level) no longer calls Cache.set to clear the stepwise cache when stepwise is inactive — it returns early instead.
In xdist worker processes, StepwisePlugin.pytest_sessionfinish no longer calls Cache.set to persist the lastfailed list — it returns early instead.
In the xdist controller process (or in non-xdist runs), both session-finish paths continue to update the stepwise cache as before.
The workerinput attribute on the Config object is used as the discriminator to identify xdist worker processes.
acceptance_criteria: When pytest is run with --stepwise and xdist (e.g., -n auto), only the controller process writes to the stepwise cache at session end; no worker process performs a cache write.
When pytest is run with xdist but without --stepwise, only the controller process clears the stepwise cache; worker processes skip the cache-clearing step.

When pytest is run without xdist (single process), the stepwise plugin's cache behavior is identical to previous versions — cache is cleared when stepwise is inactive and lastfailed is persisted when stepwise is active.
When multiple xdist workers finish sessions concurrently, no race condition or file-system contention occurs on the stepwise cache file.
Given a pytest-xdist run with many workers on a network file system, the stepwise cache remains consistent and is not corrupted by concurrent writes.

task_2.title: Show test location instead of fixture location when skipping from a fixture
task_2.description: When pytest.skip() is called inside a fixture, the short test summary info (shown with -rs) previously displayed the fixture file and line number where pytest.skip() was called. This made it impossible to identify which test was actually skipped, especially when multiple tests share fixtures that conditionally skip. The fix changes the skip reporting so that the test item's own location is shown in the summary instead of the fixture location, while preserving the original behavior for xunit-style setup fixtures.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that when a test is skipped from within a fixture (via pytest.skip()), the short test summary info displays the test's own location rather than the fixture's location. Previously, the summary line (e.g., under 'short test summary info' with -rs) showed the fixture file and line where pytest.skip() was invoked, making it impossible to determine which test was skipped when multiple tests use the same skip-triggering fixture. This fix should not alter the location reporting for xunit-style setup functions.

expectation.grounded: When a skip.Exception is raised during fixture execution in pytest_fixture_setup, the exception should carry a _use_item_location flag set to True, causing the reporting layer to resolve the displayed location to the test item rather than the fixture. This flag must not be set when the fixture function name starts with 'xunit_setup'. The skip.Exception type from _pytest.outcomes must be used for the isinstance check.
expectation.conceptual: When a test is skipped from inside a fixture, the test summary should display the test's own name and location so users can identify exactly which test was skipped. Xunit-style setup fixtures should continue to show the fixture location, as they are not tied to a single test item in the same way.

constraints.grounded: The location override must only apply to skip.Exception instances, not to other TEST_OUTCOME exceptions (e.g., failures or xfail). Xunit-style setup fixtures (those whose function name starts with 'xunit_setup') must be excluded from the location override. The cached fixture result tuple structure and the exception re-raise behavior must remain unchanged. No other exception attributes or reporting paths should be affected.
constraints.conceptual: Only skip outcomes triggered from fixtures should have their reported location changed; other test outcomes (failures, expected failures) must not be affected. Setup functions that follow xunit conventions should retain original location reporting behavior. The change must not affect test pass/fail semantics or fixture caching behavior.

behavior: When pytest.skip() is called inside a regular fixture and the test summary is displayed (e.g., via -rs), the summary line now shows the test file and test function location instead of the conftest/fixture file and line number.
When pytest.skip() is called inside an xunit-style setup fixture (e.g., setup_module, setup_class), the summary line continues to show the fixture location as before.
The skip.Exception raised from a fixture now carries a _use_item_location attribute set to True, which the reporting infrastructure uses to resolve the displayed location to the test item.
Non-skip exceptions raised during fixture setup (e.g., assertion errors, other failures) are unaffected and continue to report the fixture location.
acceptance_criteria: When a test is skipped via pytest.skip() inside a regular fixture and pytest is run with -rs, the short test summary info line should display the test file and test function name, not the fixture file and line.
When multiple tests share a fixture that conditionally skips, each skipped test should appear with its own distinct test location in the summary.
When pytest.skip() is called inside an xunit-style setup function (e.g., setup_module), the summary should still display the setup function's location, not the test location.
When a fixture raises a non-skip exception (e.g., an assertion error), the reported location should remain the fixture location, unaffected by this change.
The skip reason message should still be displayed correctly alongside the updated location in the summary output.

task_4.title: Fix race condition in JUnit XML report directory creation during parallel execution
task_4.description: When multiple pytest instances execute in parallel (e.g., invoked by an outer test runner like CTest) and write JUnit XML reports to the same parent directory, a race condition could cause intermittent failures. The issue was a time-of-check-time-of-use (TOCTOU) gap between verifying whether the output directory exists and creating it. If two instances checked simultaneously and both found the directory missing, the second call to create it would fail because the first instance had already created it. The fix makes directory creation tolerant of the directory already existing, eliminating the race window.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that JUnit XML report generation does not fail with a directory-creation error when multiple pytest instances run in parallel and target the same parent output directory. The prior behavior exhibited a race condition: between checking whether the directory exists and attempting to create it, another parallel instance could create it first, causing an unexpected OSError/FileExistsError. This must be resolved so that concurrent pytest invocations reliably produce their XML reports without filesystem race failures.

expectation.grounded: The LogXML.pytest_sessionfinish method must create the parent directory for the JUnit XML logfile using os.makedirs with exist_ok=True, so that concurrent invocations do not raise FileExistsError when the directory is created by another process between the existence check and the creation call. The method must still raise an OSError if directory creation fails for reasons other than the directory already existing (e.g., permission denied, path component is a file).
expectation.conceptual: When pytest generates JUnit XML reports, the output directory creation step must be safe for concurrent execution. Multiple pytest processes writing XML reports to the same parent directory must all succeed without interfering with each other. Directory creation failures unrelated to concurrency (such as permission errors) must still propagate as errors.

constraints.grounded: The fix must not suppress OSError conditions other than the directory already existing (e.g., PermissionError, NotADirectoryError must still propagate). If the parent path of the XML output exists as a regular file rather than a directory, the subsequent file-open call should still fail with an appropriate exception. The change must not alter behavior when pytest runs as a single instance.
constraints.conceptual: The race condition fix must be narrowly scoped to directory creation for JUnit XML output. It must not mask genuine filesystem errors. Single-instance pytest behavior must remain unchanged. The fix should not introduce new dependencies or alter the JUnit XML output format.

behavior: When multiple pytest processes concurrently attempt to create the same JUnit XML output directory, all processes succeed without raising FileExistsError.
When the JUnit XML output directory already exists before pytest_sessionfinish runs, directory creation is silently skipped and report writing proceeds normally.
When the JUnit XML output directory cannot be created due to permission errors or invalid path components, an OSError is still raised.
When a single pytest instance runs, JUnit XML report generation behaves identically to before the fix.
The TOCTOU window between checking directory existence and creating the directory is eliminated by performing an atomic create-if-not-exists operation.
acceptance_criteria: When two or more pytest processes run in parallel and are configured to write JUnit XML reports to the same parent directory, all processes should complete successfully and produce their respective XML report files without FileExistsError.
When pytest runs with --junitxml pointing to a path whose parent directory does not yet exist, the directory should be created and the XML report written successfully.
When pytest runs with --junitxml pointing to a path whose parent directory already exists, the XML report should be written successfully without any directory-creation error.
When the parent path for the JUnit XML output cannot be created due to insufficient permissions, pytest should raise an appropriate OSError.
When a single pytest instance generates a JUnit XML report, the output should be identical to previous behavior with no observable difference.

task_1.title: Fix importlib.abc.TraversableResources deprecation warning on Python 3.12
task_1.description: On Python 3.12, importing pytest triggers a DeprecationWarning because the assertion rewriting hook references importlib.abc.TraversableResources, which is deprecated in Python 3.12 and scheduled for removal in Python 3.14. The fix updates the import to use importlib.resources.abc.TraversableResources on Python 3.12+ while preserving the existing import path for older Python versions, eliminating the spurious deprecation warning.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that importing pytest on Python 3.12+ does not emit a DeprecationWarning about 'importlib.abc.TraversableResources' being deprecated and slated for removal in Python 3.14. Previously, the AssertionRewritingHook class referenced the deprecated importlib.abc.TraversableResources symbol at class-body evaluation time, causing a warning to be raised whenever the _pytest.assertion.rewrite module was loaded.

expectation.grounded: On Python 3.12+, the AssertionRewritingHook.get_resource_reader method must use TraversableResources imported from importlib.resources.abc instead of importlib.abc. On Python 3.10 and 3.11, it must continue to use importlib.abc.TraversableResources. No DeprecationWarning with the message 'importlib.abc.TraversableResources is deprecated' should be raised when importing _pytest.assertion or any pytest module on Python 3.12+.
expectation.conceptual: Importing pytest on Python 3.12 or later must complete without emitting any deprecation warnings related to importlib.abc.TraversableResources. Behavior on Python 3.11 and earlier must remain unchanged.

constraints.grounded: The AssertionRewritingHook class must still implement get_resource_reader on Python 3.10+ and return a valid TraversableResources-compatible object. The version-conditional import must correctly branch at the Python 3.12 boundary. No new warnings or import errors may be introduced on any supported Python version.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must not break resource loading behavior for any supported Python version. The assertion rewriting hook must continue to function correctly as both a MetaPathFinder and Loader. No deprecation warnings from internal pytest imports should be observable by users on any supported Python version.

behavior: On Python 3.12+, TraversableResources is imported from importlib.resources.abc instead of importlib.abc, avoiding the DeprecationWarning triggered by accessing the deprecated symbol.
On Python 3.10 and 3.11, TraversableResources continues to be imported from importlib.abc, maintaining existing behavior.
The get_resource_reader method's return type annotation references the version-appropriate TraversableResources class.
Importing _pytest.assertion on Python 3.12 with warnings set to error (-W error) no longer causes a failure.
acceptance_criteria: When importing pytest on Python 3.12+, no DeprecationWarning mentioning 'importlib.abc.TraversableResources' is emitted.
When running Python 3.12 with '-W error' flag and importing _pytest.assertion, the process exits successfully without raising DeprecationWarning as an error.
When importing pytest on Python 3.10 or 3.11, behavior is identical to before the change with no new warnings or errors.
When a test module uses assertion rewriting on Python 3.12, the AssertionRewritingHook.get_resource_reader method works correctly and returns a valid resource reader.
When running the pytest meta test suite (test_no_warnings) on Python 3.12, all tests pass including the _pytest.assertion module import check.

task_3.title: Fix rootdir defaulting to filesystem root on Windows
task_3.description: On Windows, pytest could incorrectly resolve the rootdir to the filesystem root (e.g., C:\) when the common ancestor of the current working directory and the test path resolved to the drive root. This happened because the filesystem-root detection logic compared the drive-relative portion of the path against a hardcoded Unix separator rather than the platform-appropriate separator. The fix introduces a dedicated helper function that uses the OS-native path separator, ensuring that the filesystem root is correctly detected on both Windows and Unix, and that pytest falls back to the ancestor path instead of using the drive root as rootdir.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that pytest does not use the filesystem root directory (e.g., C:\ on Windows) as the rootdir when the current working directory and the test arguments reside on the same drive but share no common directory beyond the drive root. Previously, the filesystem root detection failed on Windows because it checked for a Unix-style separator, causing pytest to keep the drive root as rootdir and generate cache artifacts (e.g., C:\.pytest_cache) in an undesirable location.

expectation.grounded: The determine_setup function in _pytest.config.findpaths must detect when the computed common ancestor is the filesystem root on all platforms. A new is_fs_root(p: Path) function must use os.sep to perform the root check instead of a hardcoded forward slash. When is_fs_root returns True for the computed common ancestor, determine_setup must fall back to the ancestor path derived from the test arguments rather than retaining the filesystem root as rootdir.
expectation.conceptual: When pytest computes the rootdir and finds that the common ancestor of the working directory and the test paths is the filesystem root, it should detect this condition correctly regardless of operating system and fall back to a more appropriate directory (the ancestor of the provided test arguments) instead of using the filesystem root.

constraints.grounded: The is_fs_root function must use os.path.splitdrive combined with os.sep to determine whether a path is the filesystem root. The existing behavior on Unix (where os.sep is '/') must remain unchanged. The fallback logic that replaces rootdir with the ancestor path when the root is detected must continue to apply in determine_setup.
constraints.conceptual: The fix must be cross-platform: it must continue to work correctly on Unix/macOS (where the root is '/') while also working on Windows (where roots are drive-letter-based, e.g., 'C:\'). No existing rootdir resolution behavior for non-root common ancestors should be altered.

behavior: On Windows, when the common ancestor of CWD and test argument paths resolves to a drive root (e.g., C:\), the filesystem root detection now correctly identifies this as a root path.
When the filesystem root is detected as the common ancestor, determine_setup falls back to using the ancestor of the provided test arguments as rootdir instead of the drive root.
A new is_fs_root utility function encapsulates the filesystem root check using os.path.splitdrive and os.sep for platform-correct behavior.
On Unix/macOS, behavior is unchanged since os.sep is '/' which matches the previous hardcoded value.
The .pytest_cache directory is no longer created at the filesystem root on Windows in scenarios where CWD and test paths share only the drive root as a common ancestor.
acceptance_criteria: When pytest is invoked on Windows with a CWD and test argument paths that share only the drive root as a common ancestor (e.g., CWD='C:\Code\project' and args='C:\Users\...\Temp\...\project'), the resolved rootdir should be the test argument ancestor, not the drive root.
When pytest is invoked on Unix with CWD and test paths whose common ancestor is '/', the rootdir should fall back to the test argument ancestor, not '/'.
When pytest is invoked with CWD and test paths that share a common directory deeper than the filesystem root, rootdir resolution should behave exactly as before (no regression).
The is_fs_root function should return True for filesystem root paths on both Windows (e.g., 'C:\') and Unix (e.g., '/'), and return False for non-root paths on both platforms.
No .pytest_cache directory should be generated at the filesystem root when the rootdir fallback logic is triggered.
